History and Physical (H&P) Clinical Note

History:
- Presenting complaint: Blinding headache ongoing for three days.
- Onset: Sudden, began upon waking three days ago.
- Duration: Persistent; present all day with temporary, partial relief from Ibuprofen.
- Severity: Mostly 8/10, occasionally drops to 5/10.
- Location: Diffuse, worst over right eye.
- Associated symptoms: Light sensitivity (photophobia), occasional "shooting lights" in vision, mild nausea (no vomiting), difficulty focusing, disrupted ability to work.
- No: Numbness/tingling, weakness, sore throat, ear pain, sinus tenderness, cough, nosebleeds, weight change, fever, or previous similar visual symptoms.
- No nocturnal awakening from headache; can sleep, but wakes with headache.
- Worse with sudden standing or moving head quickly.
- No recent travel.
- Family history: Mother has migraines with vomiting.
- Social: Lives alone, non-smoker, drinks alcohol (~once weekly), no recreational drugs.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic illnesses, no significant previous headaches (past isolated event in youth, self-resolved).
- Medications: Combined oral contraceptive pill (name not documented, started one year ago), Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented) for headache.
- No known allergies.
- Recent normal vision exam.
- Blood pressure checked ~1 year ago; reportedly normal.

Physical Examination:
- No objective findings documented (consult conducted remotely).
- Patient alert, able to converse.
- No signs of acute infection or neurological deficit reported by patient.
- No throat swelling or signs of sinus involvement.
- No fever reported or checked.

Impression:
- First episode of severe persistent headache with visual symptoms, possible migraine.

Management Plan:
- Prescribed stronger analgesic (name/dose/route/frequency not documented), and advised concomitant Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Advised to take pain medications with food.
- Arranged follow-up for in-person neurological examination, including fundoscopy and blood pressure check.
- Patient advised to continue current contraceptive pill, with review pending headache diagnosis.
- Advised to attend emergency department if headache worsens, changes in character, or becomes unbearable prior to scheduled appointment.

Patient Summary:
- Patient presents with first severe, persistent headache with visual symptoms, unresponsive to Ibuprofen. Features suggest new-onset migraine, but full neurological assessment is planned to rule out other causes. Supportive symptomatic management initiated and monitoring in place.

Key Takeaways:
- Start prescribed pain medication (stronger than Ibuprofen) as directed, with Paracetamol if needed.
- Book/attend follow-up exam for neurological assessment and blood pressure check.
- Seek urgent (A&E) care if headache acutely worsens or new symptoms develop.

Next Steps:
- Book in-person appointment for neurological assessment including fundoscopy and blood pressure measurement.
- Continue current medications pending further review unless advised to stop.
- Consider change of contraceptive pill if migraine with aura confirmed.
- Escalate to emergency care if headache becomes severe or there are neurological changes.

Quality checks:

●	Missing clinically expected elements:
  - Medication and dosage details for new prescription not specified.
  - Details of the oral contraceptive pill (name/dose) not documented.
  - Vitals and direct physical examination findings unavailable due to remote format.
  - Formal neurological examination pending.
  - Formal allergy and medication reconciliation could be more explicit.

●	Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - None identified.

●	Transcript quality:
  - Audio quality noted as occasionally poor at start but did not limit clinical data collection. Patient’s responses generally clear, minimal missing information.
